title: Which rectangles cannot be cut into two or three identical squares?
description: Two rectangles are chosen that break the rule for cutting into two identical squares and the rule for three. Keeko's doubt is that any rectangle can be cut into two identical squares.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rectangle gives two identical squares only if its length is twice its breadth, and three only if it is three times, so other sides fail. Watch for students who think any rectangle can be cut into identical squares.

source: Give the lengths of the sides of a rectangle that cannot be
video_script.why: A learner uses the length and breadth rules for two and three identical squares to choose rectangles that break them.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question asking for the sides of a rectangle that cannot be divided into two identical squares, and of one that cannot be divided into three
video_script.anchor: two rectangles drawn on the board with a question mark over each, one for two squares and one for three squares
video_script.wrong_answer: any rectangle can be cut into two identical squares
video_script.wrong_move: assumes every rectangle can be cut down the middle into two identical squares

final_answer.value: a) for example 4 cm by 2.5 cm, b) for example 7 cm by 2 cm

maths_rules: two identical squares: length = 2 times breadth
4 cm by 2.5 cm: 2 times 2.5 cm = 5 cm, and 4 cm is not 5 cm, so it cannot be cut into two identical squares
three identical squares: length = 3 times breadth
7 cm by 2 cm: 3 times 2 cm = 6 cm, and 7 cm is not 6 cm, so it cannot be cut into three identical squares
video_script.design: The two rules are stated, then each is broken with a chosen pair of sides and checked.

beats.on_screen: title card, then two blank rectangles with a question mark over each

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the two rectangles are drawn
marks.ask: the question marks appear over the rectangles

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the sides of two rectangles.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>One rectangle must not split into two identical squares, and the other must not split into three. When can a rectangle split into two identical squares?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two rules: 2 squares, length = 2 times breadth; 3 squares, length = 3 times breadth

marks.two: a rectangle of two squares is drawn, with its length as twice its breadth
marks.three: a rectangle of three squares is drawn, with its length as three times its breadth

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>A rectangle splits into two identical squares only when its length is twice its breadth.
<bookmark mark='three'/>It splits into three identical squares only when its length is three times its breadth.

beats.on_screen: Given: the rule for 2 squares and the rule for 3 squares
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one rule for two squares and another rule for three squares.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sides of a rectangle that breaks each rule

marks.find: the task is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to give sides that break each rule.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: for two squares, choose a length that is not 2 times the breadth

marks.choose: a plan appears: pick a length that is not twice the breadth

narration: <bookmark mark='choose'/>Step one, for two squares, choose a length that is not twice the breadth.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: try 4 cm by 2.5 cm; 2 times 2.5 cm = 5 cm, and 4 cm is not 5 cm

marks.try: a rectangle of 4 cm by 2.5 cm is drawn
marks.twice: twice the breadth is shown as 5 cm, longer than the 4 cm length

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step two, try four centimetres by two point five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Twice two point five centimetres is five centimetres, and four centimetres is not five centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: for three squares, try 7 cm by 2 cm; 3 times 2 cm = 6 cm, and 7 cm is not 6 cm

marks.try: a rectangle of 7 cm by 2 cm is drawn
marks.thrice: three times the breadth is shown as 6 cm, shorter than the 7 cm length

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step three, for three squares, try seven centimetres by two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='thrice'/>Three times two centimetres is six centimetres, and seven centimetres is not six centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a) 4 cm by 2.5 cm, b) 7 cm by 2 cm (other answers are possible)

marks.res: the two rectangles glow with their sides

narration: <bookmark mark='res'/>Four centimetres by two point five centimetres cannot make two squares. Seven centimetres by two centimetres cannot make three.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two rectangles
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the 4 cm by 2.5 cm rectangle with one 2.5 cm square cut off and a 1.5 cm strip left over

marks.doubt: a line is drawn down the middle of the 4 cm by 2.5 cm rectangle
marks.fix: the two parts are measured and are not squares
marks.keep: one square of 2.5 cm fits and a 1.5 cm strip is left

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks any rectangle can be cut into two identical squares.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But cut the four by two point five rectangle down the middle, and the parts are not squares.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>One square of two point five centimetres fits, and a strip of one point five centimetres is left.
